//: Template listing every configuration key the API reads, with empty values.
This file is documentation only - it is never loaded by the application.
Real values go in one of three places, never in a committed file:
- docker compose    : the .env file next to docker-compose.yml
Any key can be supplied as an environment variable by replacing ':' with '__',
Cors__AllowedOrigins__0. Array entries are indexed from 0.
Sections marked REQUIRED have no default: the application validates them at
startup and refuses to boot if they are missing or malformed.

ConnectionStrings.//ApplicationDbContext: REQUIRED. SQLite connection string. Local: 'Data Source=kodis.db'. Server: an absolute path on local disk, e.g. 'Data Source=/var/lib/kodisapi/kodis.db'. Never a network volume - SQLite allows a single writer and does not tolerate remote filesystems.

Sqids.//Alphabet: REQUIRED. Shuffled alphabet used to encode a notebook's integer id into its public slug. At least 16 characters, no duplicates. Shuffle your own; changing it later invalidates every slug already handed out. Not a security boundary, but deployment-specific - do not publish it.
Sqids.//MinLength: Minimum slug length, 4-32. Longer slugs are harder to guess. Default 8.

Google.//ClientId: REQUIRED. OAuth 2.0 client id from the Google Cloud console. Every Google credential presented to the sign-in endpoints must have been issued to this client, or it is rejected. A client id is public by design (the browser sends it) - the client *secret* is not used by this API at all. Add the frontend's origins to the client's authorised JavaScript origins.

JwtSettings.//Secret: REQUIRED, SECRET. HMAC-SHA256 signing key for both access and refresh tokens. At least 32 characters. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 48. Anyone holding this value can mint tokens for any user - never commit it, and rotate it if it leaks (which signs every user out).
JwtSettings.//Issuer: 'iss' claim stamped into every token and required when validating one. Default 'kod.is'.
JwtSettings.//Audience: 'aud' claim stamped into every token and required when validating one. Default 'kod.is'.
JwtSettings.//AccessExpirationTimeInMinutes: Access token lifetime, 1-1440. Also the window during which a logged-out session's access token still validates, since bearer validation is stateless. Default 15.
JwtSettings.//RefreshExpirationTimeInMinutes: Refresh token lifetime, 1-525600. Slides forward on every successful refresh, so an active session stays alive and an abandoned one ages out. Default 20160 (14 days).
JwtSettings.//ClockSkewInSeconds: Tolerance for clock drift between this server and its clients, 0-300. Default 60.

Cors.//AllowedOrigins: REQUIRED, at least one entry. Browser origins allowed to call the API, exact scheme + host + port. Production: 'https://kod.is'. Development also needs the Vite dev server, 'http://localhost:5173'.

Notebook.//AnonymousLifetimeInHours: How long a notebook created without signing in stays readable, 1-8760. Enforced on every read, so it takes effect immediately. A signed-in user's @username notebook ignores this and never expires. Default 24.
Notebook.//MaxNotesPerNotebook: Maximum notes in one notebook, 1-1000. Default 100.
Notebook.//MaxNoteTitleLength: Maximum note title length, 1-50. The database column is capped at 50, so this cannot usefully be raised beyond it. Default 50.
Notebook.//MaxNoteContentLength: Maximum characters in one note's content, 1024-1000000. Default 100000.
Notebook.//CleanupIntervalInMinutes: How often the background service purges expired notebooks and login sessions, 1-1440. Default 60.
Notebook.//CleanupGraceInHours: Delay between a notebook expiring (stops being served) and being physically deleted, 0-8760. The gap is deliberate: it leaves time to notice a misconfiguration before data is unrecoverable. Default 24.

Database.//MigrateOnStartup: Apply pending EF migrations on boot. Safe only for a single instance - with more than one, migrate from the release pipeline instead and leave this false. Defaults to true in Development.

Hosting.//UseHttpsRedirection: Enable only when this process terminates TLS itself. Behind a reverse proxy that handles TLS (the production setup), leave it false: the middleware would do nothing except log a warning on every request.

DataProtection.//KeyRingPath: Optional. Directory where ASP.NET Core data-protection keys are persisted, e.g. '/var/lib/kodisapi/keys'. Left unset, the framework falls back to ephemeral in-memory keys and warns on every start. Nothing currently depends on data protection; setting it keeps the logs clean and avoids a surprise later.

LogLevel.//: Standard ASP.NET Core logging configuration. 'KodisApi' controls this application's own categories.

//AllowedHosts: Host header filter, semicolon-separated. '*' accepts anything; production pins it to the real hostnames.
